comments.author: aaronm04
comments.text: Thinking can't become a hobby if you can't buy food because AI took your job.

comments.author: Two9A
comments.text:
Quite. I understand the general argument made: textiles factories meant the end of the weaver and tailor except as specialisms, livestock farming meant the end of the hunter except as a specialism, so these models will end up doing our thinking for us except as a specialism.

Even putting aside the fact that the models don't do any thinking: that doesn't help the weaver in 1850 to keep from starving, and it doesn't help those of us who've yet to surrender their cognition to keep from starving now.

comments.author: lumi
comments.text:
Even if one assumes that GenAI will become so "smart" that this is the case, we can band together against it. We are the humans on this planet and we can collectively decide what we want and what we don't want.

GenAI is squarely in the "don't want" category, and so should be fought against.

comments.author: Internet_Janitor
comments.text:
I'm increasingly resigned to spending the coming years working very hard to rebuild slop-free alternatives to rotting open-source projects, pouring energy into community-building and education, and in general thanklessly contributing a few threads of a safety net for the gigantic mess our civilization's demented oligarchs have made and are hungrily expanding.

I will never forget the people who chose to side with the oligarchs instead of humanity, who chose to torch the slow-built commons for fleeting personal convenience, attention, and enrichment. I am incandescent with anger over everything that has been pointlessly ruined, and all the lifetimes of effort it will take to clean up the oil spill.

I'll still do my part to help clean it up. There will be many of us helping.

comments.author: lumi
comments.text:
I feel we need to take this even further, we need to make alternative, ethical and sustainable ecosystems. We need a new kind of free software, one with of course the 4 essential freedoms, but also with strong communities around them that are inclusive and celebrate diversity, oppose GenAI, fascism and other similar bs, and care about the wider world.

Community is the most important thing of a software project. We need to foster strong communities with strong ethical stances.

comments.author: WilhelmVonWeiner
comments.text:
From the early 2022 fumbling release of ChatGPT, which couldn’t correctly count the number of a’s in my name (it claimed two), we reached OpenAI’s release of math papers where an internal AI model solved many hundreds of previously open math problems.


It does occur to me this is a false dichotomy: the two problems are different classes of problems. The number of times a letter occurs in a word is problem of tokenisation, lossy input, a problem of the lack of symbolic reasoning that exists with these machines, a problem of a lack of actual thought, a lack of articulation. Solving maths problems is a word game, a language problem, something LLMs are well-suited to do (especially with code to solve the symbolic thinking they can't do).

Other than that I generally agree, we're fucked to be ideas guys and doing stuff will be as unproductive as a twang off the wrist. Total human extinction will seem like the benevolent choice.
